mobs.name: Angorodon
mobs.description:
Angorodons are dangerous saurians from the Tarnished Coast that are usually found in groups. Their use of life stealing and other armor-ignoring AoE damage makes them quite deadly especially if they choose to focus on one party member.
Interrupting their key skills, denying the corpses to prevent the use of Putrid Explosion or using "Can't Touch This!" to prevent touch skills such as Twisting Jaws is advised.

mobs.name: Albino Rat
mobs.description: The Albino Rat is a charmable animal found in many areas in the Depths of Tyria. It looks like the Jahai Rat except for its white fur, red eyes and larger size. Albino Rats, pale due to the lack of pigment in their skin, eyes, and fur, are the largest known rodents on Tyria and will "eat anything and live long, healthy lives."

mobs.name: Arachni
mobs.description: Arachni is a powerful arachnid found at the end of Arachni's Haunt.

mobs.name: Arachni's Spoils
mobs.description: Arachni's Spoils will spawn after defeating Arachni in the final level of the Arachni's Haunt dungeon. Each player in the party may open the chest and will receive one item from the drop list in normal mode (2 in hard mode). After the chest has been opened by every player, a countdown timer will begin and the party will be transported outside the dungeon after three minutes.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

mobs.description: Am Fah Assassins are the frontline melee fighters of the Am Fah. They can be found in the Kaineng City region, often together with Am Fah Healers, Am Fah Necromancers and Am Fah Marksmen.

drops.name: Plague Idol
drops.description: The times are hard and fear conquers the hearts of mankind. With the plague on the loose, Imperial Guards are outnumbered more and more every day. The Am Fah, a street gang plotting against the imperialists and responsible for several murders and robberies, sees the plague, which turned the city into a place of terror, as a blessing. The Am Fah worship this plague, using these idols as the symbols of their worship, and are even willing to infect themselves to spread the plague's influence further.

They always stand on one foot when idle.

mobs.description: An Iboga Root walks on all fours like an Enchanted Brambles, but lacks any sort of foliage. It has no skills but will attack with a pink/purple projectile (could be chaos damage).

drops.name: Iboga Petal
drops.description: Iboga Petals are a type of trophy item that drops from various Iboga throughout Elona. They are the leafy remains of the sentient Iboga that wander the island of Istan. They have spicy taste and often cause immediate nausea. Despite this, these leaves are a key ingredient in Pahnai Salad, and so are prized by chefs. However, the obvious danger inherent in harvesting Iboga petals makes Pahnai Salad a rare treat at best. They are also often used in sandwiches.

drops.name: Sentient Root
drops.description: Sentient Roots are the remains of the sentient plants that populate the island of Istan. It is said that these roots have extraordinary healing properties when ground into a poultice or tea, but the inherent danger in harvesting them makes experimentation difficult.

mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

The Hydras in Ascalon are found in small groups of two to four, throughout the northwest territories of Post-Searing Ascalon. These groups tend to mingle with other indigenous enemies in these areas; for example, with Stone Furies and Boulder Elementals in the Ascalon Foothills, and Charr hunting bands in the Flame Temple Corridor. drops.description:
right|400px
War in Kryta is the first storyline of Guild Wars Beyond. It includes a series of one-time quests, exclusive items, and repeatable quests. The events begin with the player as an observer to seemingly minor events and end by the player participating in an epic battle to defend Kryta from invaders.
There are two ways to go through the War in Kryta content: following an overarcing quest or without the quest. Regardless of which route you take your character must have access to both Prophecies and Eye of the North, of which one is required to have been completed. If your character has not completed Eye of the North then either The Missing Vanguard or the now-removed Wintersday Cheer and either The Knowledgeable Asura or Zinn's Task must be completed. The quest-method is quicker as it allows the player to skip some dialogues and encounters; it also directs you through each step. The do-it-yourself method gives the player a richer view of the events leading up to the conclusion. Each method has its own walkthrough:
The quests' walkthrough;
Or the original walkthrough.

drops.name: War in Kryta
drops.description:
right|400px
War in Kryta is the first storyline of Guild Wars Beyond. It includes a series of one-time quests, exclusive items, and repeatable quests. The events begin with the player as an observer to seemingly minor events and end by the player participating in an epic battle to defend Kryta from invaders.
There are two ways to go through the War in Kryta content: following an overarcing quest or without the quest. Regardless of which route you take your character must have access to both Prophecies and Eye of the North, of which one is required to have been completed. If your character has not completed Eye of the North then either The Missing Vanguard or the now-removed Wintersday Cheer and either The Knowledgeable Asura or Zinn's Task must be completed. The quest-method is quicker as it allows the player to skip some dialogues and encounters; it also directs you through each step. The do-it-yourself method gives the player a richer view of the events leading up to the conclusion. Each method has its own walkthrough:
The quests' walkthrough;
Or the original walkthrough.

mobs.name: Hydra
mobs.description: Hydras are large three-headed lizards that use potent Fire Magic. The Hydras in Ascalon are found in small groups of two to four, throughout the northwest territories of Post-Searing Ascalon. These groups tend to mingle with other indigenous enemies in these areas; for example, with Stone Furies and Boulder Elementals in the Ascalon Foothills, and Charr hunting bands in the Flame Temple Corridor. In the northern region of Dragon's Gullet, Hydra groups flock together in herds, forming lethal mobs when attacked.

mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

mobs.description: Azure Shadows are translucent, spirit-like creatures that reside in the Southern Shiverpeaks. They usually popup out of nowhere, but are sometimes already visible. They are notorious for appearing in groups of 3 or more and casting Signet of Judgment almost immediately after engaging in battle - a headache for runners without some protection against knockdown.

The protection provided by the Dolyak Masters is particularly insidious, causing the target to be healed whenever it would normally take damage.

mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

mobs.description: Summit Giant Herders are Stone Summit that have enslaved snow beasts for use as war mounts, manipulating them through the use of a complex harness made up of chains and manacles. Thus the beast's dying scream is always one of rage, not pain.

drops.name: Fetid Carapace
drops.description: Fetid Carapaces are the unhealthy looking exoskeletons from devourers in the Ascalon region.

drops.name: Half-Eaten Mass
drops.description: Half-Eaten Masses are salvage items dropped by certain Devourers in Ascalon.

drops.name: Monstrous Claw
drops.description: A Monstrous Claw is a rare crafting material that can be used in the crafting of certain armor sets.

drops.name: Poisonous Stinger
drops.description: The Poisonous Stinger is the venomous stinger of a Plague Devourer. Its poison has to be extracted in order to brew an antidote.

drops.name: The Poison Devourer
drops.description: The people of Lakeside County have discovered Devourers with poisonous stingers. Travel to their cave and get a stinger to take to Brother Mhenlo.

mobs.name: Rrrack Whitefire
mobs.description: Rrrack Whitefire is a Charr Monk boss encountered in Fort Ranik and the Eastern Frontier.

drops.name: Charr Carving
drops.description: The crude Charr Carvings are small idols left behind by vanquished Charr in Ascalon. It is not known whether they are personal charms or totems to the Charr gods, or whether there is some other significance to them, but adventurers will accumulate them in considerable numbers.

drops.name: Charr Hide
drops.description: Charr Hides are salvage items that drop from all Charr in Ascalon, both before and after The Searing.

mobs.name: Whiptail Devourer
mobs.description: Whiptail Devourers are common foes infesting the shattered countryside of Ascalon. They attack primarily by shooting projectiles with their tails. Like all devourers, they are often hidden beneath the surface of the ground, bursting from their hiding place to ambush unsuspecting prey.

drops.description: Iboga Petals are a type of trophy item that drops from various Iboga throughout Elona. They are the leafy remains of the sentient Iboga that wander the island of Istan. They have spicy taste and often cause immediate nausea. Despite this, these leaves are a key ingredient in Pahnai Salad, and so are prized by chefs. drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

mobs.name: Hydra
mobs.description: Hydras are large three-headed lizards that use potent Fire Magic. The Hydras in Ascalon are found in small groups of two to four, throughout the northwest territories of Post-Searing Ascalon. These groups tend to mingle with other indigenous enemies in these areas; for example, with Stone Furies and Boulder Elementals in the Ascalon Foothills, and Charr hunting bands in the Flame Temple Corridor. In the northern region of Dragon's Gullet, Hydra groups flock together in herds, forming lethal mobs when attacked.

drops.name: Mineral Springs
drops.description: Mineral Springs is an area in the Shiverpeaks. Its nearest outpost is The Granite Citadel, although it is not directly adjacent to it. Mineral springs has one main path which runs in a loop around the area. It is not possible to cut across the loop and the path must be followed all the way round. There are 6 Avicara boss spawns along the path, three of which have elites only obtainable from this area. To the north east there is a cave guarded by Ice Imps, Siege Ice Golems and Nightmares; at the end of the cave, the Temple of Lyssa can be found. Taking the south east exit from the cave leads to the Phantom Boss, Ice Beast, and a lake vista where the Seer is available to infuse armor. In the south-south-east, there is a small cave where Maw the Mountain Heart can (rarely) be found.

drops.name: Mineral Springs
drops.description: Mineral Springs is an area in the Shiverpeaks. Its nearest outpost is The Granite Citadel, although it is not directly adjacent to it. Mineral springs has one main path which runs in a loop around the area. It is not possible to cut across the loop and the path must be followed all the way round. There are 6 Avicara boss spawns along the path, three of which have elites only obtainable from this area. To the north east there is a cave guarded by Ice Imps, Siege Ice Golems and Nightmares; at the end of the cave, the Temple of Lyssa can be found. Taking the south east exit from the cave leads to the Phantom Boss, Ice Beast, and a lake vista where the Seer is available to infuse armor. In the south-south-east, there is a small cave where Maw the Mountain Heart can (rarely) be found.

mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

drops.name: Mineral Springs
drops.description: Mineral Springs is an area in the Shiverpeaks. Its nearest outpost is The Granite Citadel, although it is not directly adjacent to it. Mineral springs has one main path which runs in a loop around the area. It is not possible to cut across the loop and the path must be followed all the way round. There are 6 Avicara boss spawns along the path, three of which have elites only obtainable from this area. To the north east there is a cave guarded by Ice Imps, Siege Ice Golems and Nightmares; at the end of the cave, the Temple of Lyssa can be found. Taking the south east exit from the cave leads to the Phantom Boss, Ice Beast, and a lake vista where the Seer is available to infuse armor. In the south-south-east, there is a small cave where Maw the Mountain Heart can (rarely) be found.

mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

drops.name: Mineral Springs
drops.description: Mineral Springs is an area in the Shiverpeaks. Its nearest outpost is The Granite Citadel, although it is not directly adjacent to it. Mineral springs has one main path which runs in a loop around the area. It is not possible to cut across the loop and the path must be followed all the way round. There are 6 Avicara boss spawns along the path, three of which have elites only obtainable from this area. To the north east there is a cave guarded by Ice Imps, Siege Ice Golems and Nightmares; at the end of the cave, the Temple of Lyssa can be found. Taking the south east exit from the cave leads to the Phantom Boss, Ice Beast, and a lake vista where the Seer is available to infuse armor. In the south-south-east, there is a small cave where Maw the Mountain Heart can (rarely) be found.

drops.name: War in Kryta
drops.description:
right|400px
War in Kryta is the first storyline of Guild Wars Beyond. It includes a series of one-time quests, exclusive items, and repeatable quests. The events begin with the player as an observer to seemingly minor events and end by the player participating in an epic battle to defend Kryta from invaders.
There are two ways to go through the War in Kryta content: following an overarcing quest or without the quest. Regardless of which route you take your character must have access to both Prophecies and Eye of the North, of which one is required to have been completed. If your character has not completed Eye of the North then either The Missing Vanguard or the now-removed Wintersday Cheer and either The Knowledgeable Asura or Zinn's Task must be completed. The quest-method is quicker as it allows the player to skip some dialogues and encounters; it also directs you through each step. The do-it-yourself method gives the player a richer view of the events leading up to the conclusion. Each method has its own walkthrough:
The quests' walkthrough;
Or the original walkthrough.

Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

mobs.name: Summit Giant Herder
mobs.description: Summit Giant Herders are Stone Summit that have enslaved snow beasts for use as war mounts, manipulating them through the use of a complex harness made up of chains and manacles. These "mounts" are guided through brute strength and the threat of pain rather than the traditional, time-consuming methods of breaking and training. Thus the beast's dying scream is always one of rage, not pain.

mobs.name: Master of Damage
mobs.description:
The Master of Damage is a Zaishen master, who players can test their abilities against. He informs players on various statistics about their damage. He does not attack, but instead says every five seconds the average damage you do per second to him. Damage against the two Adjacent targets that are next to him is not counted.
After you use the /bow emote, stop dealing damage or dealing damage to him for 3 minutes, he will tell you:
Total damage.
Total time.
Average damage per second.
Highest damage during a second and what second the damage was done.
Shortest time it took to kill him.
The damage total includes life stealing and health degeneration but does not include the 20% health reduction from Deep Wound.

drops.name: Iboga Petal
drops.description: Iboga Petals are a type of trophy item that drops from various Iboga throughout Elona. They are the leafy remains of the sentient Iboga that wander the island of Istan. They have spicy taste and often cause immediate nausea. Despite this, these leaves are a key ingredient in Pahnai Salad, and so are prized by chefs. However, the obvious danger inherent in harvesting Iboga petals makes Pahnai Salad a rare treat at best. They are also often used in sandwiches.

drops.description: Sentient Seeds are a type of trophy item that drops from various plants found on Istan. According to Sehyal, they are the only antidote for a love potion. mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

mobs.name: Kappa (Hatchling)
mobs.description:
Kappa at level 1 are considered hatchlings (due to the Kappa Hatchling Shells they drop). They are the weakest of the kappa species but should not be underestimated by low-level characters as their damage potential is high due to their Water Magic spells.
In Panjiang Peninsula, they are usually found together with one adult kappa, which is easily recognizable by their relative size difference.
As with other level 1 creatures, these Kappa do not aggro on sight, and will only attack when attacked. They also do not have natural health regeneration.

The Rogue Bull is an animal that requires defeating as part of the quest A Mesmer's Burden. His pet name is Bill. He belonged to Old Mac. He will respawn until you kill him with the quest active, after which he will not return.
He cannot be charmed.

mobs.name: Skale Broodcaller
mobs.description:
Skale Broodcaller are a larger and more dangerous variant of River Skale, and are always found amongst other River Skale. Skale Broodcaller have the same appearance as River Skale, but are slightly larger in size.
Unlike River Skale, Skale Broodcaller will attack unprovoked, and cause all River Skale and River Skale Tad (in the area of each party member) to attack your allies as well.

mobs.description: Plague Worms behave very similarly to other Worms in the game, except they will by default not attack and are unable to move.

drops.name: Baked Husk
drops.description: Baked Husks are the shells of the Plague Worms that infest the fields of Ascalon. The husks are used as fertilizers.

mobs.name: River Drake
mobs.description: The River Drake is the first dragon creature Tyrian characters can find. It is a good source of XP for lower level characters, as it is higher level than most Pre-Searing mobs. It is easier to tackle with a spellcaster due to Blurred Vision, but can also be dealt with by melee classes due to their higher armor rating.

mobs.name: River Skale Brood
mobs.description: The River Skale Brood is the largest and most dangerous Skale encountered in pre-Searing Ascalon. Despite its relative low-level, it has several features which make it one of the toughest creatures on the southern side of the Great Northern Wall. The Brood has extended aggro range, can heal with Aura of Restoration while striking hard with the spammable Ice Spear.

drops.name: Skale Fin (pre-Searing)
drops.description: Skale Fins are left behind by the Skale that populate the rivers and lakes of Ascalon. The skale are a menace to travelers, and Ascalonians are always glad to see anyone disposing of large numbers of Skale Fins.

mobs.name: River Skale Tad
mobs.description: River Skale Tads are juvenile River Skale and are only found amongst other River Skales. They are slightly smaller in size than grown River Skale. They will not attack players unless they are attacked or are near a Skale Broodcaller.

mobs.name: Torment Claw
mobs.description:
Torment Claws are large claws that reach up from the ground. They are usually found near rifts from the Realm of Torment into the mortal world or in the Realm itself.
Torment Claws are immobile and only possess melee range attacks, and are thus defenseless to ranged attacks; their only dangerous attack, Torment Slash, can also be avoided by staying behind or away from them.

drops.name: Mineral Springs
drops.description: Mineral Springs is an area in the Shiverpeaks. Its nearest outpost is The Granite Citadel, although it is not directly adjacent to it. Mineral springs has one main path which runs in a loop around the area. It is not possible to cut across the loop and the path must be followed all the way round. There are 6 Avicara boss spawns along the path, three of which have elites only obtainable from this area. To the north east there is a cave guarded by Ice Imps, Siege Ice Golems and Nightmares; at the end of the cave, the Temple of Lyssa can be found. Taking the south east exit from the cave leads to the Phantom Boss, Ice Beast, and a lake vista where the Seer is available to infuse armor. In the south-south-east, there is a small cave where Maw the Mountain Heart can (rarely) be found.

mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

drops.stats: Requirement, rarity, and non-inherent modifiers can vary.
drops.description: The Briar Blade is a wooden sword that drops only from plants.

drops.name: Iboga Petal
drops.description: Iboga Petals are a type of trophy item that drops from various Iboga throughout Elona. They are the leafy remains of the sentient Iboga that wander the island of Istan. They have spicy taste and often cause immediate nausea. Despite this, these leaves are a key ingredient in Pahnai Salad, and so are prized by chefs. However, the obvious danger inherent in harvesting Iboga petals makes Pahnai Salad a rare treat at best. They are also often used in sandwiches.

drops.name: Sentient Root
drops.description: Sentient Roots are the remains of the sentient plants that populate the island of Istan. It is said that these roots have extraordinary healing properties when ground into a poultice or tea, but the inherent danger in harvesting them makes experimentation difficult.

drops.name: Sentient Seed
drops.description: Sentient Seeds are a type of trophy item that drops from various plants found on Istan. According to Sehyal, they are the only antidote for a love potion. Jidun says they are also used for a mind control potion, while Paljab claims that they can be used to counteract such a potion.

drops.name: Spiritwood Plank
drops.description: A Spiritwood Plank is a rare crafting material. Nicholas the Traveler was once told that a fire that burns Spiritwood Planks is capable of comforting spirits.

drops.name: Wood Plank
drops.description: Wood Planks are a common crafting material which can be used to craft weapons and armor.

mobs.name: Frigid Skale
mobs.description: Frigid Skales are usually encountered in groups of three or singly grouped with other skales. The damage they can deal can spike a caster to death easily if a party is not careful.

drops.name: Half-Digested Boots
drops.description: Half-Digested Boots are a type of salvage item, a drop that can contain runes, insignia, and crafting materials.

drops.name: Skale Claw
drops.description: Skale Claws are trophies dropped by Istan skale.

drops.name: Skale Fin
drops.description: Skale Fins are dropped by the Skale that populate the rivers of Istan. Skale Fins are considered a delicacy by the Istani, and are prized by chefs for this reason.

drops.name: Skale Tooth
drops.description: Skale Teeth are sharp pointed fangs taken from the jaws of skale slain on Istan, as a trophy of their defeat. It is possible to exchange them on Istan for armor.

mobs.name: Irontooth Drake
mobs.description: Irontooth Drakes are found in swampy areas, mostly on their own in the earlier areas. The later areas see several of them grouped together. In the Plains of Jarin, two of them are usually found by many small groups of Juvenile Bladed Termites; they are not grouped together and the insects can be pulled and killed without attracting the drake.

drops.name: Chunk of Drake Flesh
drops.description: A piece of drake meat with skin still attached to it.

drops.name: Half-Digested Armor
drops.description: Half-Digested Armor is all that remains of previous (and less successful) heroes.

mobs.name: Istani Cultist
mobs.description: Istani Cultists look like normal Istani citizens; however, they are only seen bowing and praying to some Skale. From this it seems that the Istani Cultists believe that the Skales are holy creatures.

mobs.name: Mandragor Imp
mobs.description: Mandragor Imps are necromancers that accompany other Mandragors. They are mostly found in mandragor groups that suddenly popup as you approach them. In Kourna, some of them are always visible, but as you approach, other mandragors will popup.

drops.name: Luminous Stone
drops.description: Luminous Stones are dropped by Mandragors in Kourna and the Desolation.

drops.name: Lustrous Stone
drops.description: Lustrous Stones are salvage items left behind by the Mandragor of Istan.

drops.name: Mandragor Carapace
drops.description: Mandragor Carapaces are the woody shells of the Mandragor that ambush travelers throughout Istan. They are hard to find due to the fact that the mandragor remain hidden until they attack, and then it's usually too late. The mandragor are a menace to travelers, so the Istani are always happy to see someone disposing of a large quantity of their carapaces.

drops.name: Mandragor Root
drops.description: The Mandragor Root is a trophy dropped by mandragors in Kourna. It is one of a few trophies that can be traded for sweet points all year long.

drops.name: Mandragor Swamproot
drops.description: Mandragor Swamproots are roots from Mandragors which are said to "grow into vines that, if planted properly along a hillside, latch onto the soil and keep it from eroding." They are also used in sandwiches.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

drops.name: Mineral Springs
drops.description: Mineral Springs is an area in the Shiverpeaks. Its nearest outpost is The Granite Citadel, although it is not directly adjacent to it. Mineral springs has one main path which runs in a loop around the area. It is not possible to cut across the loop and the path must be followed all the way round. There are 6 Avicara boss spawns along the path, three of which have elites only obtainable from this area. To the north east there is a cave guarded by Ice Imps, Siege Ice Golems and Nightmares; at the end of the cave, the Temple of Lyssa can be found. Taking the south east exit from the cave leads to the Phantom Boss, Ice Beast, and a lake vista where the Seer is available to infuse armor. In the south-south-east, there is a small cave where Maw the Mountain Heart can (rarely) be found.

drops.name: Scale
drops.description: Scale is categorized as a common crafting material, though it is on the rare side of the common materials. Scales should not be confused with Skale, which is a monster species.

mobs.name: Juniper Bark
mobs.description: Juniper Barks are plant creatures that populate the Shiverpeak Mountains. They spend most of their time just below the surface of the ground, but pop up to attack when enemies come near. While not particularly dangerous by themselves, when they appear during a battle with other, more dangerous creatures, they cease to be a mere nuisance and become a true threat.

drops.name: Alpine Seed

mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

The Margonites are the primary demonic servants of Abaddon; chosen and favored with his divine blessing.
Before the Exodus of the Gods, the Margonites were a seafaring nation of humans that had settled in and around the Crystal Sea, later transformed into ethereal demons by Abaddon. In their demonic form, the Margonites have a natural life span that has been seen to reach to over one thousand years, as evidenced by Lord Jadoth's being older than 1076 years. According to The Lost, their long life and demonic powers come at the price of sterility, thus the Margonites can only increase their numbers by transforming others into Margonites.
Margonites, even after their demonic transformation, are capable of individual thinking. Two examples of this are The Lost and Apostate, who decided to betray Abaddon.

mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

mobs.name: Keiran Thackeray
mobs.description:
Lieutenant Keiran Thackeray is an officer of the Ebon Vanguard and leader of the Ebon Falcons, and grew up around Drascir. He made his first appearance during the Wintersday 1078 AE celebrations, when he was left in charge of the Eye of the North. During his time in charge, he went to great lengths (or more accurately, enlisted the help of hapless players to go to great lengths for him) to cheer up a lonely Gwen.
In the time since then, a romance has developed between the two of them, however for a time this was on hold after Gwen's refusal to celebrate her own birthday led to a falling-out between the pair. He was then dispatched, along with Captain Langmar and the rest of his unit, to Kryta to help the Shining Blade in their civil war in exchange for Krytan aid against the Charr, with words left unsaid between him and Gwen. Although his role was mainly limited to training new recruits, during the Battle for Lion's Arch, he bought Ascalon settlers time to escape to the relative safety of the capital by helping to divert White Mantle forces, along with Captain Langmar and Captain Greywind. He did not return after the battle, and was listed as missing in action. A devastated Gwen, now in command of the Ebon Vanguard, used one of his bows and the Scrying Pool to locate him, witnessing the events that followed the battle.
Traveling through Kryta, a bedraggled Thackeray encountered Miku, with whom he hunted down and killed Danthor the Adamant. The two then pursued the remaining White Mantle forces to their base in the Maguuma Jungle, where they discovered a plan to massacre Beetletun and place the blame on the Shining Blade. They returned to the town and Thackeray used his newfound leadership skills to rally townspeople to fight the Mantle, and together they successfully repelled the attack. With his potential as a Paragon now realized, Miku invited him to join her on her return to Cantha, but Thackeray declined, instead opting to return to the Vanguard. Eventually, he made his way to the Shiverpeaks, and at Anvil Rock he was reunited with Gwen. After returning to the Eye of the North to recover, he proposed to Gwen, and the two were married in Olafstead.

mobs.name: Ghost

right|200px
Most restless souls of formerly living creatures have some sort of reason for hanging around a place: an unfinished task, a wrong that needs righting, and so on. They're often coherent, and you can hold a reasonable conversation with them—the few not eager to have you join them, at least. mobs.name: spawn
mobs.description:
right|thumb|200x|A Spawn Ring, as seen in Shing Jea Monastery.
Spawning is appearing on a map. This can be players or NPCs appearing at a specified point under a certain condition, e.g. when a point is reached that was set to spawn a group of enemies.
Spawn/spawn(ing) point:
The set points on the map that foes, NPCs, allies, etc. are scripted to appear.
A group of such creatures that appear at such a point; an alternate form of mob.
Less frequently, the term is applied to players -- only in the form spawn(ing) point:
The points at which players appear on a map after transit, which may not be adjacent to the portals they came through (sometimes referred to as zoning). Also, the starting point of a mission, the initial locations of players on a PvP map.
The points where dead players reappear in PvP matches; also: "respawn point".
mobs.movement_notes: when a point is reached that was set to spawn a group of enemies. A group of such creatures that appear at such a point; an alternate form of mob.

drops.name: War in Kryta
drops.description:
right|400px
War in Kryta is the first storyline of Guild Wars Beyond. It includes a series of one-time quests, exclusive items, and repeatable quests. The events begin with the player as an observer to seemingly minor events and end by the player participating in an epic battle to defend Kryta from invaders.
There are two ways to go through the War in Kryta content: following an overarcing quest or without the quest. Regardless of which route you take your character must have access to both Prophecies and Eye of the North, of which one is required to have been completed. If your character has not completed Eye of the North then either The Missing Vanguard or the now-removed Wintersday Cheer and either The Knowledgeable Asura or Zinn's Task must be completed. The quest-method is quicker as it allows the player to skip some dialogues and encounters; it also directs you through each step. The do-it-yourself method gives the player a richer view of the events leading up to the conclusion. Each method has its own walkthrough:
The quests' walkthrough;
Or the original walkthrough.

drops.name: War in Kryta
drops.description:
right|400px
War in Kryta is the first storyline of Guild Wars Beyond. It includes a series of one-time quests, exclusive items, and repeatable quests. The events begin with the player as an observer to seemingly minor events and end by the player participating in an epic battle to defend Kryta from invaders.
There are two ways to go through the War in Kryta content: following an overarcing quest or without the quest. Regardless of which route you take your character must have access to both Prophecies and Eye of the North, of which one is required to have been completed. If your character has not completed Eye of the North then either The Missing Vanguard or the now-removed Wintersday Cheer and either The Knowledgeable Asura or Zinn's Task must be completed. The quest-method is quicker as it allows the player to skip some dialogues and encounters; it also directs you through each step. The do-it-yourself method gives the player a richer view of the events leading up to the conclusion. Each method has its own walkthrough:
The quests' walkthrough;
Or the original walkthrough.

drops.name: Mineral Springs
drops.description: Mineral Springs is an area in the Shiverpeaks. Its nearest outpost is The Granite Citadel, although it is not directly adjacent to it. Mineral springs has one main path which runs in a loop around the area. It is not possible to cut across the loop and the path must be followed all the way round. There are 6 Avicara boss spawns along the path, three of which have elites only obtainable from this area. To the north east there is a cave guarded by Ice Imps, Siege Ice Golems and Nightmares; at the end of the cave, the Temple of Lyssa can be found. Taking the south east exit from the cave leads to the Phantom Boss, Ice Beast, and a lake vista where the Seer is available to infuse armor. In the south-south-east, there is a small cave where Maw the Mountain Heart can (rarely) be found.

mobs.name: Grawl
mobs.description:
right|200px
The Grawl are humanoid creatures roaming Tyria from the Charr Homelands to the southern areas of the Shiverpeak Mountains. This species has an ape like physique and seems to possess a primitive form of culture with a social hierarchy and different professions.
While the Grawl are seen fighting beside the Charr quite often, there is no clear evidence that they are allies. The only sign of organized cooperation between the two was working alongside Vatlaaw Doomtooth and later an attempt to form an alliance by Torch Harrowkeeper. Galton Franks, a collector for the Ebon Vanguard, seems to believe that "the grawl are either proto-Charr or, more likely, an important source of Charr nutrition".
While the exact nature of their religious beliefs are unknown, Durmand believes that their necklaces hold some evidence for their religious tendencies. Along with that, the Grawl seem to congregate at a few locations with statues to the Gods of Tyria - such as at Melandru's statue at King's Watch, Lyssa's statue outside the Ruins of Surmia outpost, and outside the Temple of Grenth.
In Regent Valley, there are groups of Grawl who fight each other: the Grawl Petitioners and Grawl Heretics. These two groups indicate a form of civil or religious split.
As theorized by Nicholas Sandford, the number of necklaces worn by a grawl may indicate a special status or strength. Nicholas further speculates that the Grawl have to outnumber the necklaces worn before they can attack.
mobs.movement_notes: The Grawl are humanoid creatures roaming Tyria from the Charr Homelands to the southern areas of the Shiverpeak Mountains.

They are often found in groups of three with at least one Grawl Shaman, especially in The Northlands.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

drops.name: War in Kryta
drops.description:
right|400px
War in Kryta is the first storyline of Guild Wars Beyond. It includes a series of one-time quests, exclusive items, and repeatable quests. The events begin with the player as an observer to seemingly minor events and end by the player participating in an epic battle to defend Kryta from invaders.
There are two ways to go through the War in Kryta content: following an overarcing quest or without the quest. Regardless of which route you take your character must have access to both Prophecies and Eye of the North, of which one is required to have been completed. If your character has not completed Eye of the North then either The Missing Vanguard or the now-removed Wintersday Cheer and either The Knowledgeable Asura or Zinn's Task must be completed. The quest-method is quicker as it allows the player to skip some dialogues and encounters; it also directs you through each step. The do-it-yourself method gives the player a richer view of the events leading up to the conclusion. Each method has its own walkthrough:
The quests' walkthrough;
Or the original walkthrough.

Regardless of which route you take your character must have access to both Prophecies and Eye of the North, of which one is required to have been completed. If your character has not completed Eye of the North then either The Missing Vanguard or the now-removed Wintersday Cheer and either The Knowledgeable Asura or Zinn's Task must be completed. The quest-method is quicker as it allows the player to skip some dialogues and encounters; it also directs you through each step. The do-it-yourself method gives the player a richer view of the events leading up to the conclusion. Each method has its own walkthrough:
The quests' walkthrough;
Or the original walkthrough.

mobs.name: Beastmaster Korg
mobs.description:
Beastmaster Korg can be found in a northern section on the second level of Rragar's Menagerie. He can be seen standing at the top of a flight of stairs, seemingly alone. When approached, a group of Fleshreavers spawn at the foot of the stairs.
Due to lacking a surname, it is not known which High Legion Beastmaster Korg belonged to, let alone which warband other then Rragar's hypothetical Man warband.

mobs.name: Fleshreaver Harrower
mobs.description: Fleshreaver Harrowers are ritualists that serve mostly as light damage and healing support for Fleshreavers. Beware of their Spirit Rift in Hard mode, as it can do massive damage to clustered parties.

drops.name: Fleshreaver Morsel

mobs.name: Fleshreaver Hound
mobs.description: Fleshreaver Hounds are monks that provide hex and condition removal to their squads, while doing massive area of effect holy damage. They appear in large numbers and will tend to cast Ray of Judgment on the same targets, potentially doing huge damage to clustered parties, especially in Hard mode.

drops.name: Fleshreaver Morsel
drops.description: Fleshreaver Morsels are hunks of flesh torn from Fleshreavers. They can be fed to Blobby.

mobs.name: Fleshreaver Nephilim
mobs.description: Fleshreaver Nephilim are paragons that can do respectable damage with their attacks and inflict numerous conditions on opponents. When in the same squads as Fleshreaver Harrowers, the Harrowers will spread Cracked Armor on your party so that the Nephilim will both do more damage and consistently inflict Deep Wound.

drops.name: Fleshreaver Morsel
drops.description: Fleshreaver Morsels are hunks of flesh torn from Fleshreavers. They can be fed to Blobby.

mobs.name: Hidesplitter
mobs.description: Hidesplitter is Rragar Maneater's ultimate Fleshreaver creation, and is one part of the boss-like duo in the Rragar's Menagerie dungeon. He does massive physical damage with his attacks, which are further augmented by Rragar's use of The Master's Mark.

drops.name: Fleshreaver Morsel

mobs.name: Hidesplitter's Chest
mobs.description: Hidesplitter's Chest will spawn after defeating Rragar Maneater and Hidesplitter in the final level of the Rragar's Menagerie dungeon. Each player in the party may open the chest and will receive one item from the drop list in normal mode (2 in hard mode). After the chest has been opened by every player, a countdown timer will begin and the party will be transported to Doomlore Shrine after three minutes.

mobs.name: Banished Dream Rider
mobs.description:
Banished Dream Riders are spectral horsemen and powerful mesmers that can be seen wandering the Chaos Planes in the Underworld as well as the Rift. They are servants of Dhuum.
In the Underworld they sometimes appear to be alone, but their deaths will spawn a group of three Mindblade Spectres. Killing those Mindblades will then be followed by a new spawn of six Mindblades and then further on by a spawn of nine Mindblades. Some Banished Dream Riders can also be found in groups of two with a Wailing Lord. When in a group Banished Dream Riders do not spawn Mindblades.
In the ruins of the Tomb of the Primeval Kings they can be found accompanied by Terrorweb Dryders, Scythes of Chaos and Grasps of Insanity. These Banished Dream Riders do not spawn Mindblade Spectres.

drops.name: Mineral Springs
drops.description: Mineral Springs is an area in the Shiverpeaks. Its nearest outpost is The Granite Citadel, although it is not directly adjacent to it. Mineral springs has one main path which runs in a loop around the area. It is not possible to cut across the loop and the path must be followed all the way round. There are 6 Avicara boss spawns along the path, three of which have elites only obtainable from this area. To the north east there is a cave guarded by Ice Imps, Siege Ice Golems and Nightmares; at the end of the cave, the Temple of Lyssa can be found. Taking the south east exit from the cave leads to the Phantom Boss, Ice Beast, and a lake vista where the Seer is available to infuse armor. In the south-south-east, there is a small cave where Maw the Mountain Heart can (rarely) be found.

drops.description: Tattered Fan is a unique focus item dropped by Jade Brotherhood Ritualists and Shen, the Magistrate, foes who can be found in Wajjun Bazaar.

drops.name: Wajjun Bazaar
drops.description: Wajjun Bazaar is a busy and prosperous seafront in central Kaineng. A variety of goods and services are available here, since local imports make their way to the other parts of Kaineng from here. The Am Fah have made inroads from the Undercity into this area and control much of the southern roads and alleys, much to the annoyance of the Jade Brotherhood whose guild hall is on the island in the northwest.

mobs.name: Fendi's Chest

mobs.name: Locked Chest
mobs.description:
Locked Chests are chests found in hard mode instances in Prophecies, Factions, and Nightfall and in all explorable areas (including normal mode) in Eye of the North. They can only be opened using a lockpick. Opening a Locked Chest adds one point to the Treasure Hunter title track in both cases.
The skins of weapons that drop from these chests are relative to the area the chest is in and also can be influenced by the mobs or the creature type/affiliation of foes around the chest itself.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

drops.description:
Info that appears in the User interface|UI after pickup.|thumb|right
The Dungeon Key is an item found in the dungeons of Eye of the North. When a player fulfils a certain requirement, usually killing a boss in a dungeon, a key will appear on the ground. The key is color matched to its own door. You need to use a key on a Dungeon Lock near to door.

mobs.name: Duncan the Black
mobs.description: Duncan the Black is the final boss in the only elite dungeon, Slavers' Exile. He is an extremely powerful Ritualist, with a large amount of health. After he is defeated, a Hierophant's Chest appears. Duncan has hired guardians to protect him while he harvests the powers of the Great Destroyer for his own evil designs.

mobs.name: Forgewight
mobs.description: Forgewight is a powerful fire Elemental serving as one of Duncan the Black's henchmen. After he is defeated a Chest of the Slaver (Forgewight) appears.

mobs.name: Hierophant's Chest
mobs.description: The Hierophant's Chest will spawn after defeating Duncan the Black in the final level of the Slavers' Exile dungeon. Each player in the party may open the chest and will receive one Deldrimor Armor Remnant, one Onyx Gemstone and one random item from the drop list below (2 in hard mode). After the chest has been opened by all party members, a three minute countdown timer will begin, after which players will be transported out of the dungeon.

mobs.name: Justiciar Thommis
mobs.description:
Justiciar Thommis is an important White Mantle member, and one of its founders. He saw his allies murdered and Saul D'Alessio kidnapped by the Mursaat, but chose to remain silent and instead become one of the most influential people in Kryta.
Following the events of the Divinity Coast mission, his brother Rhynnon is killed by the Shining Blade. Avenging Rhynnon's death is the objective of the quest A Brother's Fury.
Thommis survived the reemergence of the Titans, and can be found in Slavers' Exile under the employ of Duncan the Black.

mobs.name: Rand Stormweaver
mobs.description: Rand Stormweaver is a bosslike foe found in the northeast corner of Justiciar Thommis's room of Slavers' Exile. He is accompanied by a small group of Stone Summit dwarves, and a patrol of Wretched Wolves occasionally passes by his location. When he is defeated, a Chest of the Slaver (Rand Stormweaver) appears at his spawn location.
mobs.movement_notes: He is accompanied by a small group of Stone Summit dwarves, and a patrol of Wretched Wolves occasionally passes by his location.

mobs.name: Selvetarm
mobs.description:
Selvetarm is a Dryder boss-like foe found at the end of one of the levels of Slavers' Exile. He is joined by a group of Stone Summit dwarves, and pairs of Shock Phantoms, Crypt Wraiths, and Crypt Slashers circle his room.
When defeated, a Chest of the Slaver (Selvetarm) appears at his spawn location, and four Restless Dead (Shadow Prison version) around it.
mobs.movement_notes: He is joined by a group of Stone Summit dwarves, and pairs of Shock Phantoms, Crypt Wraiths, and Crypt Slashers circle his room.

drops.name: Mineral Springs
drops.description: Mineral Springs is an area in the Shiverpeaks. Its nearest outpost is The Granite Citadel, although it is not directly adjacent to it. Mineral springs has one main path which runs in a loop around the area. It is not possible to cut across the loop and the path must be followed all the way round. There are 6 Avicara boss spawns along the path, three of which have elites only obtainable from this area. To the north east there is a cave guarded by Ice Imps, Siege Ice Golems and Nightmares; at the end of the cave, the Temple of Lyssa can be found. Taking the south east exit from the cave leads to the Phantom Boss, Ice Beast, and a lake vista where the Seer is available to infuse armor. In the south-south-east, there is a small cave where Maw the Mountain Heart can (rarely) be found.

mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

drops.name: Mineral Springs
drops.description: Mineral Springs is an area in the Shiverpeaks. Its nearest outpost is The Granite Citadel, although it is not directly adjacent to it. Mineral springs has one main path which runs in a loop around the area. It is not possible to cut across the loop and the path must be followed all the way round. There are 6 Avicara boss spawns along the path, three of which have elites only obtainable from this area. To the north east there is a cave guarded by Ice Imps, Siege Ice Golems and Nightmares; at the end of the cave, the Temple of Lyssa can be found. Taking the south east exit from the cave leads to the Phantom Boss, Ice Beast, and a lake vista where the Seer is available to infuse armor. In the south-south-east, there is a small cave where Maw the Mountain Heart can (rarely) be found.

mobs.name: Stone Summit Gnasher
mobs.description:
Stone Summit Gnashers are the minion masters of the Stone Summit. If left unchecked, they are capable of raising a large minion army that will pose a significant threat to the party. In Guild Wars Eye of the North, their updated skill bar makes them even more effective minion masters.
The best way to deal with them is to take them down as early as possible. Alternatives would be to prevent them from exploiting corpses or to bring skills that are devastating to minions or summoned creatures (such as Avatar of Balthazar, Verata's Aura, and Holy Spear, to name a few). Also, abusing their use of Plague Touch can draw them into the middle of your group, effectively separating them from their group, making it easy to take them out first.

mobs.name: Lord Jadoth
mobs.description: Lord Jadoth, also referred to as The General, was once a human Margonite alive before the Exodus of the Gods. For unknown reasons, he was hunted down by the Forgotten and exiled to the Crystal Sea. During his exile, when the Forgotten's armada approached his refuge, he called upon Abaddon for salvation and became the first Margonite blessed with magic by Abaddon in 1 BE. He is said to be a great tactician. He currently resides within the City of Torc'qua in the Realm of Torment, he began serving Mallyx the Unyielding as one of the four Lords of Anguish upon Abaddon's defeat.

mobs.name: Banished Dream Rider
mobs.description:
Banished Dream Riders are spectral horsemen and powerful mesmers that can be seen wandering the Chaos Planes in the Underworld as well as the Rift. They are servants of Dhuum.
In the Underworld they sometimes appear to be alone, but their deaths will spawn a group of three Mindblade Spectres. Killing those Mindblades will then be followed by a new spawn of six Mindblades and then further on by a spawn of nine Mindblades. Some Banished Dream Riders can also be found in groups of two with a Wailing Lord. When in a group Banished Dream Riders do not spawn Mindblades.
In the ruins of the Tomb of the Primeval Kings they can be found accompanied by Terrorweb Dryders, Scythes of Chaos and Grasps of Insanity. These Banished Dream Riders do not spawn Mindblade Spectres.

mobs.name: Kanaxai
mobs.description:
Kanaxai is a chaos demon of nightmaresGuild Wars Factions Prima Guide who dwells within the Deep, beneath the Jade Sea. He is the leader of the Nightmare Horde comprised of Nightmares, Oni, and the maddened Outcasts. His exact origins and allegiances are unknown, though rumors across Cantha suggest his Oni come from the Mists,Conflict in Cantha though others speculate Oni are transformed Outcasts.Dauv Merishahl According to rumors, the Oni first appeared shortly after the Jade Wind, which was when Kanaxai was trapped beneath the sea.Andru PitrakEurayle
When Luxon Reavers delving deep into the Jade for high quality deposits discovered him, his influence drove them mad. They became Outcasts, and they now serve as minions of his growing Nightmare Horde.Outcasts in the QuarryJefri Whylir

mobs.name: The Leviathan
mobs.description:
The Leviathan is a giant wurm found in the area with the Aspect of Shadows inside The Deep. It can fire a powerful projectile attack that does high damage, often 300 damage or more.
In addition to the environmental effect of not being able to cast enchantments in most of the area, the Leviathan will be surrounded by several Reborn Irukandji which will keep placing the Spirit of Disenchantment making Protection Prayers and other protective enchantments nearly useless.
Upon approaching it, the Leviathan will be encased in jade, but will break free as soon as players come close enough.

drops.name: Rhea's Crater
drops.description: Rhea's Crater lies on the eastern end of the Jade Sea. The whole of the area appears to be a large Luxon quarry with deep excavation works being carried out in multiple places. The unearthed jade stands as a grim reminder of the day the Jade Sea became frozen, as the preserved remains of fish, serpents, and other aquatic life forms can be seen within the jade blocks. The southern part of this area are narrow and deep pathways riddling through blocks of jade. The northern and middle portions are on higher ground with ledges where mining works are being carried out. The middle area also contains a small flooded section in the east. This area is crawling with Jade Sea wildlife and the Outcasts maintain long and fast patrols throughout this area.

mobs.name: Banished Dream Rider
mobs.description:
Banished Dream Riders are spectral horsemen and powerful mesmers that can be seen wandering the Chaos Planes in the Underworld as well as the Rift. They are servants of Dhuum.
In the Underworld they sometimes appear to be alone, but their deaths will spawn a group of three Mindblade Spectres. Killing those Mindblades will then be followed by a new spawn of six Mindblades and then further on by a spawn of nine Mindblades. Some Banished Dream Riders can also be found in groups of two with a Wailing Lord. When in a group Banished Dream Riders do not spawn Mindblades.
In the ruins of the Tomb of the Primeval Kings they can be found accompanied by Terrorweb Dryders, Scythes of Chaos and Grasps of Insanity. These Banished Dream Riders do not spawn Mindblade Spectres.

drops.name: Elemental Keystone
drops.description:
The Elemental Keystone is a bundle dropped by selected foes in Forsaken Tunnels and Tunnels of the Forsaken. When carried near the associated crystal wall, it will cause it to collapse, opening the way to the rest of the dungeon.
In Tunnels of the Forsaken, it opens the way to the 2nd floor portal.
In Forsaken Tunnels, it opens the way to the 3rd floor portal, as well as the two areas where the boss Maz escapes during the final fight.

drops.name: Charr Bag
drops.description:
A Charr Bag is an equippable item that provides 10 additional inventory spaces. Because they already hold 10 items, they cannot be upgraded by using a Rune of Holding. A Superior Rune of Holding can be applied to it after leaving Pre-Searing and make it hold 15 items. A character may wear up to 2 bags at one time. Bags are not visible to other players.
Charr Bags are most commonly used by players in Pre-Searing who, without access to storage, have little inventory space.

drops.name: Charr Carving
drops.description: The crude Charr Carvings are small idols left behind by vanquished Charr in Ascalon. It is not known whether they are personal charms or totems to the Charr gods, or whether there is some other significance to them, but adventurers will accumulate them in considerable numbers.

drops.name: Charr Salvage Kit
drops.description: A Charr Salvage Kit is a type of kit that provides the only method for pre-Searing characters to obtain upgrade components. They look and work the same as Expert Salvage Kits; however, they have only five uses and they can only be obtained as drops from one of the Charr bosses or Maz's Chest.

drops.name: Charr Bag

A Charr Bag is an equippable item that provides 10 additional inventory spaces. Because they already hold 10 items, they cannot be upgraded by using a Rune of Holding. mobs.name: Banished Dream Rider
mobs.description:
Banished Dream Riders are spectral horsemen and powerful mesmers that can be seen wandering the Chaos Planes in the Underworld as well as the Rift. They are servants of Dhuum.
In the Underworld they sometimes appear to be alone, but their deaths will spawn a group of three Mindblade Spectres. Killing those Mindblades will then be followed by a new spawn of six Mindblades and then further on by a spawn of nine Mindblades. Some Banished Dream Riders can also be found in groups of two with a Wailing Lord. When in a group Banished Dream Riders do not spawn Mindblades.
In the ruins of the Tomb of the Primeval Kings they can be found accompanied by Terrorweb Dryders, Scythes of Chaos and Grasps of Insanity. These Banished Dream Riders do not spawn Mindblade Spectres.

mobs.name: Dhuum
mobs.description:
Dhuum was once the God of Death. During his reign, Dhuum ruled from his tower in the Underworld, and tolerated neither resurrections nor the existence of the undead, and he hunted down all those who escaped death, having promised "death undeniable."
Long before the Exodus of the Gods, Dhuum was challenged and usurped by Grenth and seven heroes who followed him and was struck down in the ossuary of the Cathedral of Eternal Radiance in Orr. Dhuum's tower was shattered, creating the Chaos Plains, and his power was transferred to Grenth, who sealed him within the Hall of Judgement behind enchanted doors and layers of divine magic as he was unable to destroy Dhuum. There, Dhuum bided his time, gaining power every time a creature dies in the Underworld. Sometime before the Flameseeker Prophecies could be realized, the upheaval in Tyria allowed the army of Dhuum to launch an assault on the Underworld, imprisoning Grenth's Reapers and taking control of large portions of the realm. Other agents of Dhuum allied with servants of Abaddon during the attack on the Tomb of the Primeval Kings, during the disruption of the 1585 CC Dragon Festival led by the Fury, and finally in the Realm of Torment during Nightfall, along with Menzies' forces.
Years later, Dhuum was able to accumulate enough power to break free of his bonds, but forces led by King Frozenwind were able to defend the Reapers long enough for them to perform a ritual to return him to his dormant state.

mobs.name: Mindblade Spectre
mobs.description:
Mindblade Spectres are ghosts that appear in the Chaos Planes of the Underworld and also during the quest Escort of Souls. Their high health, high armor rating against physical damage, and multiple interrupts supported by Migraine make them a significant threat to both spellcasters and martial classes. Protecting the Lost Souls from the Mindblade Spectres is vital for the party, since their death will result in quest failure and will kick the whole party from the Underworld.
Mindblade Spectres also appear after destroying a Banished Dream Rider. A group of three Mindblade Spectres spawn, after which a second group of six Mindblade Spectres and a third group of nine Mindblade Spectres spawn, each after the previous group has been destroyed. Your party should be aware of this before confronting any Banished Dream Riders or the fight might result in a party wipe.

mobs.name: Banished Dream Rider
mobs.description:
Banished Dream Riders are spectral horsemen and powerful mesmers that can be seen wandering the Chaos Planes in the Underworld as well as the Rift. They are servants of Dhuum.
In the Underworld they sometimes appear to be alone, but their deaths will spawn a group of three Mindblade Spectres. Killing those Mindblades will then be followed by a new spawn of six Mindblades and then further on by a spawn of nine Mindblades. Some Banished Dream Riders can also be found in groups of two with a Wailing Lord. When in a group Banished Dream Riders do not spawn Mindblades.
In the ruins of the Tomb of the Primeval Kings they can be found accompanied by Terrorweb Dryders, Scythes of Chaos and Grasps of Insanity. These Banished Dream Riders do not spawn Mindblade Spectres.
